why: The linter's test fixtures are code samples that must contain the very constructs the linter forbids -- 'var', ': any', 'as any'. Held inline they were source text in a lintable file, so the deterministic standards audit that gates every task read the suite's own test data as 16 BLOCKING violations, and the file became uneditable: any task touching it failed a gate on strings that exist to prove the gate works. Fixtures are data, not code, so they live in data. The audit reads .mjs/.cjs/.js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx only.

cases.excessive_parameters: function sendEmail(recipient, subject, body, attachment, priority) {}
cases.one_line_jsdoc_prose: /** summary: any failing check makes it FAIL */
cases.one_line_block_prose: /* summary: any failing check makes it FAIL */
cases.pragma_comment_then_violation: /* eslint-disable-next-line */ const v = u as any;
